Fitting taper equations

Source: vignettes/methods-fitting-taper.Rmd
methods-fitting-taper.Rmd

fit_taper() estimates coefficients for compiled taper forms from repeated stem measurements. as_taper_model() converts a fit into a model accepted by the stem registry.

Fitting data and forms

Required columns are tree, dbh, ht, h, and dib. Tree diameter and total height must remain constant within each tree. The shipped example_stem_measurements contains modeled diameters from example_trees, not independent field measurements.

## Select the shipped fitting measurements
measurements <- example_stem_measurements %>%
  select(tree, dbh, ht, h, dib)
tree dbh ht h dib
1 12 60 3.000 11.423
1 12 60 6.857 10.472
1 12 60 10.714 9.927
1 12 60 14.571 9.381
1 12 60 18.429 8.806
form source structure
kozak_1988 Kozak (1988), doi:10.1139/x88-213 Variable exponent with reference point
kozak_2002 Kozak (2004), doi:10.5558/tfc80507-4 Variable exponent with tree and height terms
max_burkhart Max and Burkhart (1976), doi:10.1093/forestscience/22.3.283 Segmented polynomial with fitted join points

The package supplies equation forms without published coefficient vectors. units describes the input measurements. Fitted coefficients use centimeters and meters.

Fit and inspect 

## Fit the segmented taper form
fit <- fit_taper(data = measurements,
                 form = 'max_burkhart',
                 units = 'imperial')
n rmse bias
90 0.697 0.009 
## Draw fitted diameters and residuals
plot(fit)

The fit stores coefficients, fitted values, residuals, and fit statistics. rmse is root mean squared error, and bias is mean observed minus fitted diameter. Both use centimeters.

summary() reports fit statistics and coefficients. predict() evaluates new measurement rows.

Supplying group requests a mixed-effects fit. The random effect acts on the Kozak scale parameter or the segmented form’s b1 parameter. Predictions use population coefficients when a group was absent from the fitting data.

## Predict diameters at the supplied measurement heights
predicted <- measurements %>%
  mutate(fitted_dib = predict(object = fit,
                              newdata = measurements,
                              units = 'imperial'))
tree dbh ht h dib fitted_dib
1 12 60 3.000 11.423 11.155
1 12 60 6.857 10.472 10.445
1 12 60 10.714 9.927 9.934
1 12 60 14.571 9.381 9.401
1 12 60 18.429 8.806 8.842

Register fitted coefficients

as_taper_model() creates a model from population coefficients. register_taper_model() makes it available for the current session. An explicit bark_ratio enables outside-bark calculations for the fitted model.

## Create and register a model from the fitted coefficients
local_model <- as_taper_model(x = fit,
                              id = 'example.segmented',
                              bark_ratio = 0.9)

## Make the model available for stem calculations
register_taper_model(model = local_model)
## Calculate volume with the fitted model
volumes <- example_trees %>%
  transmute(tree,
            cubic = stem_volume(dbh = dbh,
                                ht = ht,
                                model = local_model$id))
tree cubic
1 17.352
2 27.554
3 41.131
4 58.563
5 80.334
6 138.817 
## Validate and remove the session model
validate_taper_model(x = local_model)

## Remove the example registration
unregister_taper_model(id = local_model$id)

taper_model_from_coefficients() constructs the same compiled model type from a named coefficient vector. new_taper_model() constructs a model from R callbacks.
